newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher as stocks suck funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher as stocks suck funds.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Wednesday following an active exodus of funds from the banking system into the red hot stock market, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate finished at 7.208 percent against Tuesday's 6.856 finish -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper firmed to 7.50-7.75 percent against 7.00-7.50.
The stock market on Wednesday closed 0.62 percent or 57.41 points higher to reach a seven-year peak of 9,362.68.
Turnover was a voluminous T$213 billion.
Dealers said they expected the money rates to continue rising on Thursday because the stock market fever was unlikely to abate.
In the government bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9775-9800 percent against 5.9250.
